narr: Deep tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Nicholas overspread the area and led to the development of bands of very heavy rainfall. The slow motion of these bands produced copious amounts of rain which led to flash flooding across portions of southwest Alabama.
ev: Over 6 inches of rain is just a couple of hours time resulted in significant flash flooding in parts of the Lillian and Seminole areas. In Lillian, fast moving water over Highway 98 washed cars off the road. A water rescue had to be performed at the Lillian Post Office due to a person being trapped in their vehicle. County Road 99 at Pearson Branch Bridge was closed due to flooding. In Seminole, a portion of Liatrus Lane near Juniper Road caved in with a six to 10 foot sink hole.
Heavy rain caused the intersection to flooded at Hillcrest and Grelot Roads.
Numerous impassable roads due to flooding.
Williams Silvers Parkway, the east bound lanes of Canal Road, and Jubilee Point Road were all flooded in the Orange Beach area.
County Road 95 between County Road 20 and Fitzpatrick Lane was flooded.
